snippets.output: Pepto-Bismol is not a peptoid. Peptoids, or poly-N-substituted glycines, are a class of biochemicals that replicate the behavior of biological molecules.
Pepto-Bismol is a medication that contains bismuth subsalicylate as its active ingredient and is used to treat diarrhea and indigestion.

Pepto-Bismol’s name was derived from “Pepto” and “Bismol”: “Pepto” comes from “pepsin,” an enzyme involved in protein digestion, and “Bismol” comes from “bismuth,” a chemical element used in the medication. Pepto-Bismol’s name does not imply that it is chemically a peptoid.
